semver_policy.major: scoring model or step add/remove; scores no longer comparable across versions (resets the critique baseline)
semver_policy.minor: param/threshold/gate tuning that changes output but keeps comparability
semver_policy.patch: bug fix not expected to change good-run output

tool_versions.note: Pinned engine dependencies of the pipeline. A minor engine update can silently change a headless process/default (PI DrizzleIntegration no-op; Siril 1.4.2 seqplatesolve crash), so treat these as part of the pipeline contract: update side-by-side, keep the old binary, and only promote after `python -m nas_server.canary check` passes against critiques/golden_baselines.json. These are environment state, not pipeline logic — updating them is NOT a semver bump (bump only when pipeline code changes in response). SASpro 1.15.0->1.18.0 promoted 2026-06-11: canary check passed with all three golden finals BIT-IDENTICAL (zero drift); no dependency churn (numpy/numba/scipy/astropy unchanged); abe_run gained backward-compatible correction_mode kwarg.

versions.summary: Baseline snapshot of the current autoprocess pipeline.
versions.rationale: First versioned reference point for the critique-driven iteration loop. No code changes — establishes the line that subsequent runs are compared against.

versions.summary: Seven quality fixes from the first critique batch: better HDR/stretch/background gating, DB-driven routing, NBN palette restore, grader background context, and data-integrity QA flags.
versions.rationale: Gate/threshold/param/prompt tuning driven by the 19-critique batch (runs 2026-06-05/06). No scoring step added or removed and the scoring model is unchanged, so 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 critiques remain comparable.
changes: HDR gate (#84): also fire on a small intensely-blown core (near-white fraction lum>=0.98 >= 0.10%), not just a >=1% top-decile fraction — recovers HDR on compact blown cores like the M 42 Trapezium.
Stretch picker (#85): add a relative-grain (bg_noise/bg_level) tiebreaker, guarded to backgrounds above 0.04, to break ties away from grainy veralux_strong picks.
Background gate (#86): _objective_check now rejects a background step that WORSENS per-channel sky balance (sky_b/r, sky_g/r) and flags residual cast for a harder retry.
Workflow routing (#87): resolve object_type from DB targets.type before the name heuristic, fixing substring collisions (e.g. 'M 109' matching 'm 10' -> globular).

NBN palette (#88): post-NarrowbandNormalization HOO ColorSaturation restore in pi_postprocess.js so genuine Ha/OIII signal isn't left muted grey-tan (measured emission B/R 0.86-0.97 on M 42 / NGC 2244 NBN).
Grader context (#89): feed the measured background band into assess_stacked_image so it stops calling measured-correct backgrounds 'too dark'.

Data-integrity QA (#90): _data_integrity_flags surfaces wrong-field, pre-EQ pointing-spoof, and manual-source provenance issues to log/Telegram and run.log so a run isn't graded for problems it didn't cause.

versions.summary: Eight further quality fixes from re-examining the same 20-critique batch: crop/dark_enhance/noise gating, BXT-default deconvolution, S50 scale-hint injection, dense-field halo cap, per-channel grader colour context, and NBN neutralize completeness.
versions.rationale: Gate/threshold/param/default-fn/prompt tuning surfaced by a second pass over the 1.0.0 critiques. The deconvolution default swaps engine (cc_sharpen -> BXT) but the step itself is unchanged, the scoring model is unchanged, and no scoring step is added or removed, so 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 critiques remain comparable. (Recommendation #7, post-GHS sky pull, was already implemented in 1.1.x; #10 two-path HDR is deferred as a separate MAJOR initiative.)
changes: Crop gate (#1): force a crop when measured corner spread/bg > 0.40 (vignette/uneven corners), not just on low coverage — recovers vignetted finals (NGC 6914, M 83, NGC 6334).

dark_enhance gate (#2): target-aware shadow-SNR floor (5 for galaxy/nebula vs 12 otherwise) so faint outer-halo / reflection veil is lifted instead of blanket-vetoed (IC 4592, M 109, NGC 4565, NGC 6914, SH 2-273).
noise_reduction gate (#3): keep a denoise that holds SNR when the result is still grainy (sigma/bg > 0.18) instead of reverting on a marginal linear 'no improvement' (NGC 7635, SH 2-273).

deconvolution default (#4): standard-mode default is now bxt_deconvolve (full BlurXTerminator), best-in-class for SeeStar; cc_sharpen_inprocess remains the automatic fallback when PixInsight is unavailable and an explicit experiment variant (NGC 6914 star-ringing halos).
Scale hints (#5): inject S50 FOCALLEN=250mm + XPIXSZ/YPIXSZ=2.9um into manual XISF->FITS masters lacking them so ImageSolver/SPCC gets a scale seed within the factor-2 window (IC 1805).
halo_suppression cap (#6): cap reduction_level at 1 in dense star fields (clusters or >1000 detected stars) so aggressive halo reduction doesn't eat stars / darken the field (NGC 6914 Cygnus).

Grader colour context (#8): feed the measured per-channel corner-sky R/G/B balance into assess_stacked_image so the vision grader stops missing real sky colour casts (NGC 2244 NBN blue cast B/R 1.46).

NBN neutralize completeness (#9): background_neutralize now adds a residual-cast top-up that equalises sky-patch per-channel medians when a cast remains after the pivot shift (NGC 2244 NBN sky B/R 1.46).

versions.summary: Four fixes from Henry's review of the 1.2.0 reprocess batch: crop no longer over-crops small targets, no longer leaves vignetted finals uncropped, an over-bright stretch is pulled back to the per-type sky band, and SCNR no longer breaks SPCC calibration (skipped on SPCC-success) with a downstream channel-crush guard.
versions.rationale: Gate/threshold/param tuning and a conditional step skip surfaced by Henry's direct review of the 1.2.0 reprocess outputs (M 109/M 57 over-crop; NGC 6914/IC 1805/M 83 left uncropped; IC 434/SH 2-273 near-black coloured pedestal). The SCNR skip is conditional on the SPCC-success path (mirrors the existing narrowband SCNR skip) — no scoring step is added or removed and the scoring model is unchanged, so 1.2.0 and 1.3.0 critiques remain comparable.
changes: Crop over-crop floor (#102): crop_multi now enforces a native-resolution floor (short side >= max(900px, 0.45x native short)) and falls back to the largest-area candidate when the chosen candidate (usually canonical, sized from folio angular size) would downsample a small target below S50 resolution — fixes the ~76px M 57 / ~442px M 109 thumbnails.

Crop under-crop gate (#103): the post-stretch crop-force check now measures corner brightness on a stretched luminance (1/99.5 percentile + gamma) instead of linear data, and adds a black-edge band detector (>30% near-black in a 2% edge band) — recovers vignetted/stacking-border finals (NGC 6914, IC 1805, M 83) the linear-threshold gate silently passed.

Stretch background clamp (#104): after the stretch winner is picked, an additive sky-level clamp pulls the background into the per-object-type band when a variant (e.g. veralux_strong) overshoots above it, so the final sky lands in-band instead of washed bright.

SCNR-on-SPCC skip + channel-crush guard (#105): SCNR is skipped on the SPCC-success path (color_calibration applied and no .spcc_failed sentinel) because its non-linked Average-Neutral green clip breaks SPCC's linked white balance and crushes the neutral sky toward black (IC 434/SH 2-273 R=0.0/G=0.0019 'G/R=140' cast); SCNR still runs when SPCC failed or never ran. A belt-and-suspenders _guard_channel_crush at final save re-neutralises any residual coloured near-black pedestal left by a downstream step.

versions.summary: New artifact-trim crop candidate becomes the preferred crop: a stretched-luminance edge profile + noise trim that removes ragged/black/grainy edge stacking artifacts while keeping the full target, replacing canonical/LIR as the default selection.
versions.rationale: Surfaced by Henry's annotated review of IC 1805 (mosaic) and NGC 6334 crops: the strict LIR clipped the subject on tilted mosaics and canonical over-sized bordered targets, while the existing coverage maps didn't even match the stack dimensions. The new candidate is coverage-map-independent and is chosen by default; canonical/coverage/lir are still generated for the record and remain the fallback. The crop step is unchanged in identity and the scoring model is unchanged — no scoring step added or removed — so 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 critiques remain comparable.
changes: Artifact-trim crop candidate (preferred): crop_multi adds _artifact_trim_bounds — STF-stretches a luminance, then per edge scans inward and trims while the band is anomalous by EITHER brightness (median below 0.55x plateau = falloff/black band, or above plateau by 0.18 = residual gradient) OR high-frequency noise (above 1.6x interior = grainy low-frame-coverage border). Stops after a clean run, capped at 35% per edge, with a degenerate-box guard that falls back to the full frame. It keeps the FULL target while removing edge stacking artifacts and is now the default chosen candidate over canonical/LIR (which clipped tilted mosaics / over-sized bordered targets). Validated on IC 1805 master (full Heart kept, ~10% ragged bottom trimmed) and NGC 6334 (black/grainy borders removed: top 4% / bottom 25% / left 8% / right 13%). See [[feedback-crop-edge-artifacts]].

versions.summary: Alignment outliers are dropped from stacking. Each sub's TRUE plate-solved sky position/rotation is stored in the DB; subs whose solved position sits far from their panel/target siblings (off-pointing — e.g. pre-EQ ALP-spoofed coords) are flagged solve_status='outlier' and excluded at stack-selection time so they can't drag registration off the cluster.
versions.rationale: Surfaced by the IC 1805 panel-drop investigation: one pre-EQ sub (RA 69.98/DEC 20.27, ~50 deg off-pointing) was a spoofed-coordinate frame that polluted the max-frame mosaic. Frame selection changes (an off-cluster sub is now dropped), but the scoring model and every processing step are unchanged — no scoring step added or removed — so 1.4.0 and 1.5.0 critiques remain comparable for well-pointed data.
changes: Per-sub plate-solve capture: light_files gains solved_ra/dec/rot/scale + solve_status (ok|failed|outlier|NULL) + solved_at. Populated three ways — harvest the WCS the stack pipeline already solves (near-zero cost), an idle-worker eager-solve of unsolved subs, and an on-demand POST /solve/{target}. Keys association/alignment QA on TRUE solved position instead of the spoofable/colliding header OBJECT name.

Alignment-outlier flagging (sub_solver.flag_alignment_outliers): per (target/panel) group, computes a robust circular-median solved position and stamps any sub > 2.0 deg off as solve_status='outlier'. Does NOT touch the manual exclude column.

Stack-time outlier exclusion (stacker.py): subs with solve_status='outlier' are dropped from qualifying_paths after the exptime filter, gated by setting exclude_alignment_outliers (default true). This changes which frames stack — an off-pointing sub no longer enters registration/integration.

Rotation visibility (alignment_summary): surfaces per-group rot_median + rot_spread (max deviation from median, deg) from solved_rot so subs rotated relative to each other are inspectable. Informational only — alt-az field rotation is expected and corrected by registration, so rotation does not auto-exclude.

versions.summary: NBN vibrancy overhaul: the NarrowbandNormalization step now drives PI's real o3Boost (OIII boost) on the HOO palette, auto-scaled from Ha dominance, paired with a dedicated warm-gold/teal saturation preset. Fixes the muddy yellow-brown nbn output caused by two latent no-op bugs. Also: nebula stretch picker now weights sky placement over grain, the galaxy/non-nebula picker gains a grain-cap (drops any candidate >1.5x grainier than the cleanest in-band one) to stop a bright-but-grainy stretch beating a clean one, and the crop step is now a remembered manual review (Claude veto removed).
versions.rationale: Surfaced by Henry's investigation into why auto nbn runs (IC 1805, NGC 2244) came out muddy grey-tan instead of the vibrant blue-OIII / warm-Ha palette he gets by hand. Root cause: (1) the pipeline set nbn.normalizationMode, which does NOT exist in PI 1.9.3 — o3Boost sat at its 1.0 default (silent no-op); (2) the color_boost step ran with the galaxy preset because the standard param build reads step_def 'parameters' while the ontology key is 'params'. Both fixed; o3Boost auto-scaled from ha_dominance_ratio and a new nbn color_boost preset added. nbn is an aesthetic step and is NOT score-gated, so this does not affect the scoring model — 1.5.0 and 1.6.0 critiques remain comparable for non-nbn runs. Validated on IC 1805 (ratio 2.54 -> o3Boost 1.50) and Rosette (2.16 -> 1.35) trials matching Henry's reference image. The stretch-picker and crop-review changes were folded into this same entry (no separate version bump) because 1.6.0 has not yet produced any processing runs and its changes are uncommitted. Both are aesthetic/framing choices outside the score-gated model, so comparability is unaffected. See [[feedback-aesthetic-steps]], [[reference-seestar-lp-filter]], [[no-overcrop-s50]], [[crop-edge-artifacts]].
changes: NBN o3Boost lever (pi_postprocess.js): the NarrowbandNormalization block now sets nbn.palette=0 (HOO) and nbn.o3Boost=job.nbn_o3_boost (the real OIII-boost property), dropping the dead nbn.normalizationMode assignment that was a silent no-op in PI 1.9.3. o3Boost is the lever that surfaces the teal-blue OIII core; left at 1.0 it produced muddy yellow-brown.

Ratio-driven o3Boost (auto_process.py): narrowband_norm auto-scales o3Boost = clamp(0.50 + 0.395*ha_dominance_ratio, 1.25, 1.7) — a more Ha-dominant target gets more OIII boost to surface its weak teal core. Curve fitted to IC 1805 (2.54->1.50) and Rosette (2.16->1.35) visual sweet spots. Manual overrides nbn_o3_soft(1.3)/nbn_o3_strong(1.7). Measured ratio + chosen boost are logged per run for iteration.

NBN color_boost preset (seti_astro.py + auto_process.py + ontology): new 'nbn' color_boost preset (gold/copper dust 35deg/+0.40, amber bleed 18deg/+0.22, teal OIII core 195deg/+0.32, global_sat_lift 0.06) is routed in explicitly whenever narrowband_norm is forced — fixing the latent params/parameters key-mismatch bug that silently left nbn runs on the galaxy preset. This is now the SOLE saturation pass for nbn; the in-JS HOO ColorSaturation restore is disabled (hoo_boost=0) to avoid double/triple saturation.

Threaded params: nbn_o3_boost + nbn_hoo_boost through pixinsight.run_postprocess (signature + job dict); o3_boost + hoo_boost through seti_astro.narrowband_normalize. The /narrowband_norm branch endpoint method= now means auto (ratio-scaled) | soft (1.3) | strong (1.7) instead of the dead MaximumStars/Equalize.

Nebula stretch picker (auto_process._physics_pick_stretch): for nebula object_types the pick is now dominated by sky placement — the variant whose background sits closest to the per-type band with the least under-exposed/blown clipping wins (key = round((bg_dist+under+blown)/0.02)), and relative grain only breaks ties within that bucket. Previously grain could win outright and select an STF-overshoot variant that washed the sky bright. Galaxy/other types keep their existing picker. See [[galaxy-stretch-darker]], [[faint-nebula-too-dark]].

Crop is now a remembered manual review (Claude veto removed): on a target's FIRST auto-process the crop step opens a manual review (crop_review.py) presenting all crop_multi candidates (artifact-trim / canonical / coverage / intersection / LIR) each with an STF preview, plus a Cropper.js editor to draw/rotate a custom crop. The user's choice is persisted per target (target_crop.py / target_crops table) as a WCS sky-box (center RA/Dec + on-sky size + PA, primary) with fractional bounds + rotation as a no-WCS fallback, and reused on every later run via reproject onto the saved box (canonical_frame.reproject_to_canonical) — identical framing every session regardless of mosaic canvas growth. The old _claude_confirm_crop / _claude_crop_clips_subject vision veto is deleted. Review honors the standard grace->park->wait queue pattern (5-min grace, then releases the queue and waits indefinitely). See [[no-overcrop-s50]], [[crop-edge-artifacts]].

Crop clear/redo controls: per-target saved crop can be cleared from the target page ('Clear & redo crop' button -> POST /target/{target}/clear-crop) so the next run re-opens the review, and a per-run 'Re-crop (force fresh crop review)' queue flag (re_crop on /queue + queue-view add-job checkbox) forces a one-off fresh review without clearing the stored crop. Manual-crop geometry (incl. rotation) is persisted from the apply-crop endpoint, which knows the exact applied box.

Galaxy/non-nebula stretch grain-cap (auto_process._physics_pick_stretch): before the blended-cost sort, drop any candidate whose grain (bg_noise + 0.25*rel_grain) exceeds 1.5x the cleanest IN-BAND candidate's grain, then pick lowest cost among survivors. Fixes the M 51 6/9 regression where veralux (grain 0.248) beat the cleaner stat_bright (0.145) — both ON-TARGET sky — because veralux's brighter midtones lowered its under-exposure term more than noise_w*bg_noise penalized its grain; the final noise score tanked to 5.5 and a non-degradation restore had to ship an earlier checkpoint. Reference grain is taken from in-band candidates only, so a uniformly-grainy field (no clean in-band option) is left untouched. Distinct from the nebula picker change above (nebulae de-weight grain because their corners hold real Ha; galaxies need the opposite). See critiques 20260609_021519_seestar_galaxy + 20260604_143439_seestar_galaxy, [[galaxy-stretch-darker]].

versions.summary: Three crop/queue bug fixes. (1) Manual crop rotation no longer leaves black corner wedges: the apply-crop endpoint and the saved-crop fractional fallback now rotate-then-crop (sample the rotated source directly into the axis-aligned output box) instead of crop-then-rotate-with-reshape. (2) Park-on-review now actually advances the queue: a parked crop review releases PIPELINE_LOCK while it waits on the user, so the next queued target runs instead of stalling on the lock. (3) A user-chosen crop is never discarded by objective stats: crop is the user's explicit framing choice from the manual review (or the persisted saved crop), so it is now fully exempt from both the post-step SNR stats-veto and the force_apply objective gate. Cropping reframes the image, so a whole-frame SNR before/after comparison is meaningless anyway.
versions.rationale: Bug fixes, not expected to change good-run output → patch. (1) Henry added a small rotation in the Cropper.js editor and the result wouldn't 'reset to a rectangle' — the old path cropped the axis-aligned box first, then scipy.ndimage.rotate(reshape=True, cval=0) rotated that box inside a larger canvas, leaving zero-filled triangular wedges. Fixed in target_crop.rotated_crop() (shared by main.py apply-crop and target_crop._apply_frac_crop) via scipy.ndimage.affine_transform that inverse-maps each output pixel into the rotated source, filling the whole box with real pixels; rotation direction preserved (matches prior scipy.ndimage.rotate(-rotate), Cropper +angle=CW). The WCS sky-box reuse path was already correct (folds rotation into PA). (2) When M 31's crop review grace elapsed it parked (released the queue slot) but its auto_process thread kept holding PIPELINE_LOCK at crop_review ev.wait(); the worker popped M 51, which logged 'starting' then blocked ~40 min on PIPELINE_LOCK until M 31 fully finished. Fix: PIPELINE_LOCK now tracks its owner thread (auto_process.mark/clear/release/reacquire helpers); crop_review._await_decision releases it on park and re-acquires before resuming, so a parked (idle) review never blocks other local autoprocess work while still serializing real PI execution. Laptop worker runs auto_process without the lock, so release is owner-guarded (no-op there). (3) Surfaced by Henry asking 'did it discard my crop?' for M 51: its coverage edge-crop (rotate=0, no wedges) was force-applied by geometry, then the generic post-step SNR stats-veto reverted it because whole-frame SNR dropped 102.7→59.0 (0.57, below the 0.85 guard) and logged 'crop — no improvement, skipped'. Henry's directive: 'Don't veto crop. I am choosing it.' Crop is now fully exempt from objective gating — _objective_check('crop') returns ok/improved=True, and the post-step stats-veto skips step_name=='crop' entirely. A crop the user chose in the manual review is always applied; the pipeline never second-guesses framing with stats.
changes: Crop rotation wedge fix: new target_crop.rotated_crop(data, cx, cy, cw, ch, rotate_deg) uses scipy.ndimage.affine_transform to extract a cw×ch axis-aligned box from the rotated source — no black wedges. Replaces crop-then-ndrotate(reshape=True, cval=0.0) in main.py /review/{id}/apply-crop and target_crop._apply_frac_crop. Direction matches the old -rotate convention (verified ≤1px against scipy.ndimage.rotate).

Park-advance fix: PIPELINE_LOCK gains owner tracking (auto_process._pipeline_lock_owner + mark_pipeline_lock_held / clear_pipeline_lock_held / release_pipeline_lock_for_park / reacquire_pipeline_lock_after_park). queue_manager._run_job and main.py autoprocess set/clear the owner around their `with PIPELINE_LOCK`. crop_review._await_decision releases the lock when a review parks and re-acquires after the user responds, so the queue's next local job runs immediately instead of stalling on the lock held by the idle parked thread.

Crop objective-gate exemption: a user-chosen crop is never discarded by stats. auto_process._objective_check('crop') now returns ok=True/improved=True (framing, not gated), and the post-step SNR/gradient stats-veto skips step_name=='crop' (guard `and step_name != 'crop'`). Previously the 0.85 SNR guard reverted legitimate coverage/edge crops (M 51: 102.7→59.0) and logged 'crop — no improvement, skipped'. Crop is the user's explicit manual-review choice and is now always applied.

versions.summary: Galaxy workflow: detail-first stretch selection + masked sky mute. (1) The physics stretch picker gains a galaxy branch that ignores ALL sky terms (bg_dist, bg_noise, rel_grain, grain-cap) and selects on highlight health (under/blown, bucketed 0.05) + dead-channel reject, tie-broken by a faint-preserving preference order (mas > veralux_strong > veralux > stat_bright > stat > stf > ghs family). (2) PI MaskedStretch output is normalized to 0-1 (it writes int32-scaled FITS), so mas is finally a real candidate. (3) The galaxy path's post-combine sky mute is replaced by sky_mute_masked: an auto-tuned luminance mask (sigma-clipped sky, smoothstep sky+1.5sigma to sky+5sigma, gaussian feather, dilate blend) protects the extended galaxy while a black-point lift darkens only the sky. color_boost's existing midtone lum-mask blend already luminance-gates saturation (verified: mas M 51 mask lower 0.194 vs sky 0.149 - only the galaxy's ~10% of pixels boosted). (9) green_cap_masked: masked signal-only green-excess cap on the linear starless layer for galaxies (amount 0.7) - fixes the post-SPCC lime cast without touching the SPCC-neutral sky. (10) galaxy color_boost gains a 340deg Ha/HII pink band (+0.22 sat, +8% red lift) for visible HII knots in spiral arms.
versions.rationale: Henry's directive from the M 51 mas review: 'the key is to pick the good galaxy stretch and not worry about the sky' - galaxy detail looked awesome on mas but the picker could never choose it: (a) MaskedStretch wrote unnormalized int32 FITS (values to 4.27e9) so stats were garbage, and (b) even normalized, the sky terms killed it - mas/veralux leave the sky high (big bg_dist) and the 1.6.0 grain-cap cut them on sky-corner sigma, crowning ghs_strong, which crushes the faint arms/tidal bridge. Since sky_mute_masked darkens the sky AFTER stars are recombined, sky placement at stretch time is no longer the picker's problem; only galaxy-detail retention matters. Selection is physics-only (no Claude API call - Henry's explicit constraint) and validated against an in-session vision ground truth on 4 galaxies: M 51/M 81/M 101 -> mas, NGC 4565 -> veralux family (its mas is nearly black; the highlight-health gate rejects it and the preference order picks veralux_strong) - 4/4 reproduced offline. The old flat _mute_sky multiplied the whole frame down, dimming faint outskirts with the sky; the masked version keeps galaxy luminance untouched (M 51: sky 0.018->0.001, galaxy coverage 11.6%). Minor bump: gate/param tuning + step implementation swap on the existing sky_mute slot; no scoring step added/removed, scores remain comparable.
changes: Stretch picker galaxy branch (auto_process._physics_pick_stretch): for object_type containing 'galaxy', drop bg_dist/bg_noise/rel_grain/grain-cap entirely; sort by (round((under+blown)/0.05), _GAL_PREF index) where _GAL_PREF = [mas, veralux_strong, veralux, stat_bright, stat, stf, ghs_strong, ghs, ghs_soft]. Dead-channel reject still applies. Nebula and non-galaxy branches unchanged.

MAS normalization (auto_process._run_mas): PI MaskedStretch writes int32-scaled FITS (BITPIX=32, BZERO=2147483648); after _pi_pp returns, if max > 1.5 the data is divided by its max, clipped to 0-1, written back float32 with BZERO/BSCALE/DATAMIN/DATAMAX stripped. Without this, mas stats read p99~2.8e9 and the variant could never win.

sky_mute_masked (seti_astro): new function - luminance L = 0.2126R+0.7152G+0.0722B; sigma-clipped sky (5 iters, clip at med+2.5sigma); mask smoothstep from sky+1.5sigma to sky+5sigma; gaussian feather sigma 3; dilation blend (max_filter*0.5+M*0.5) to protect halo edges; black-point lift bp=sky-1sigma via (x-bp)/(1-bp); composite M*orig+(1-M)*dark. Returns sky_before/sky_after/galaxy_coverage.

Galaxy combine tail (auto_process): after combine_stars_screen, galaxy targets route to sky_mute_masked instead of the flat _mute_sky scale; step record stays 'sky_mute'. Non-galaxy types keep the existing _mute_sky behavior.

color_boost: NO code change - the existing _lum_mask_blend midtone mask (lower = clamp(median*1.3, 0.08, 0.30), computed from the post-stretch image) already luminance-gates saturation; measured on mas M 51 it boosts only the galaxy (9.8% of pixels above mask lower).

color_boost delta smoothing (seti_astro.color_boost): the hue-Gaussian saturation delta is now gaussian_filter(sigma=4) smoothed before applying. Hue is noisy in faint regions, so the per-pixel delta flipped adjacent pixels between the +0.30 blue boost and the -0.05 yellow damp, posterizing the color into hard orange/purple patches (Henry's zoomed M 51 report). Smoothing the boost FIELD (not the image) keeps luminance detail intact while the saturation transition becomes spatially gradual; verified on the M 51 mas stretch (speckle gone at sigma 4, blue arm boost preserved).

Manual crop editor apply fix (main.review_apply_crop + target_crop.cropper_box_to_array): the preview is flipped vertically for north-up stacks (CDELT2>0) and Cropper.js reports x/y in the rotated bounding-canvas frame, but apply-crop mapped both straight into the unflipped/unrotated array - every manual crop landed mirrored/displaced (M 31 -17deg, M 42 0deg). New mapping un-rotates the canvas box center, un-flips the row, negates the rotation angle in array space, then scales to full resolution. Poisoned saved crops for M 31/M 42 cleared.

Sky-only gradient metric (image_analyzer._background gradient_severity_sky + auto_process gate/scoring): the all-cells gradient metric is dominated by grid cells sitting on the target, so background_extraction was REJECTED on M 81 even though GraXpert flattened the sky perfectly (span 0.00022->0.00003; metric 0.176->0.248 because SPCC's bg_anchor dropped the denominator pedestal) - the leftover gradient was then amplified 9x by the mas stretch into the hazy 'green cast' top. New metric measures flatness over the object-excluded bg_cells only (M 81: 0.085->0.006 - correctly accepted); the BE/background_neutralize gate, the physics gradient score, AND the generic post-step stats veto now prefer it (the veto was a second independent guard on the old metric — it reverted the M 81 GraXpert result even after the gate fix). The weak sky_mute on M 81 (sky sigma +/-0.066) was a downstream symptom of the same uncorrected gradient.

green_cap_masked (seti_astro + auto_process star_split hook, galaxies only): SPCC's linked white balance neutralises the sky but left the galaxy SIGNAL ~10% green-heavy on S50 OSC data (M 81 trace: sky-subtracted galaxy G/R 1.04-1.12 post-SPCC where an Sab bulge should be ~0.9); the mas stretch then amplified it into the lime/yellow-green cast the grader scored color_balance 3.5. New step runs on the linear STARLESS layer right after star split: feathered luminance mask, SKY-SUBTRACTED green cap G_sig -> min(G_sig, (R_sig+B_sig)/2) at amount 0.7 (Henry's pick from the A/B; G/R 1.10 -> 1.00, warm cream bulge + blue arms). versions.summary: NBN vibrancy restored: fix the silent revert of the nbn saturation pass. (1) pi_postprocess.js 'Ensure Float32' used SampleFormatConversion.To32Bit — 32-bit UNSIGNED INTEGER, not float — so when the gate fired, PI saved full-range uint32 FITS (0..4.29e9); changed to ToFloat. (2) _lum_mask_blend now normalizes out-of-range inputs to [0,1] before computing the luminance mask — on raw uint32 data the midtone mask (0.15-0.85 band) evaluated to 0 everywhere and the blend silently replaced the step output with its input. (3) The nbn color_boost preset is exempted from the midtone lum-mask blend entirely: the pathfound vibrant SHO look (IC 1805 / Rosette trials 2026-06-08) was generated unmasked, and the mask's upper bound (~0.85) would exclude the bright cores where the restored saturation matters most; galaxy/nebula presets keep the mask. (4) narrowband_normalize gains a safety net that rewrites any non-float or out-of-range PI output as normalized float32 before returning it to the pipeline. Plus the three approved critique recommendations: (5) NEW hdr_core_blend — masked-core HDR blend with clipped-hue chroma refill, added to BOTH galaxy and nebula workflows, stats-veto-exempt; (6) folio-aware nebula stretch pick — placement key charges distance outside the folio bg_level_range; (7) NEW sky_green_rebalance — sky-only masked green cap (max(R,B), smoothed excess), SPCC-safe SCNR substitute.
versions.rationale: The 1.7.0 NBN runs on IC 1805 (5.8) and NGC 2244 (7.2) rendered steel-grey instead of the pathfound vibrant gold/teal SHO variants (IC_o3_1p5_sat / RO_o3_1p3_sat, 2026-06-08). Root cause: the NBN step input was a non-float working copy, the JS 'Float32' fix-up actually converted to uint32, and the nbn color_boost (the SOLE saturation pass, hoo_boost=0 by design) was then fully reverted by a mask computed on un-normalized uint32 luminance — bit-identical output confirmed on both runs while the step recorded 'applied'. NBN itself balances Ha/OIII to near-neutral (bright-region saturation 0.402 -> 0.198), so losing the restore pass is what produced the muted palette. The original critiques mis-framed this as an NBN palette inversion; the SHO palette is the intended aesthetic (aesthetic steps are not score-gated). ALSO IN 1.8.0: the three approved 2026-06-10 critique recommendations — (5) hdr_core_blend (M 42 + M 31: global HDR crushes faint signal and gets vetoed; masked blend touches only the core; galaxy path previously had NO HDR step), (6) folio-aware nebula stretch pick (M 42: mas sky 0.122 was in the wide per-type band 0.06-0.16 but 42% over the folio band [0.05,0.09], cost -0.2), (7) sky_green_rebalance (M 31 sky G/R 1.12, M 42 1.06 left unpolished by the SPCC-skips-SCNR rule; verified 1.045->1.012 and 1.061->1.010 with object/star color untouched; full SCNR on SPCC data stays forbidden, IC 434 precedent).

versions.summary: NBExtract + SSSC (SASpro 1.18 features): true narrowband workflow for LP dual-band data plus spectrophotometric color calibration. (1) NBExtract — xp_channel_extract unmixes TRUE Ha/OIII channels from LP stacks via a Gaia-XP mixing-matrix NNLS fit (SEP detect -> WCS->XP library match -> raw-aperture photometry -> per-star expected line fluxes -> fit A; two-phase: A is fit on the star-full post-color_calibration image, NNLS-applied to the STARLESS linear image at the stretch boundary so the channels are nebula-only). (2) nb_palette composites the extracted channels into HOO / Foraxx / synthetic-SHO (s_mix=0.8) variants — force_only aesthetic step with 4 experiment variants, replacing the old narrowband_norm Ha~R/OIII~B approximation when forced. (3) SSSC — sssc_calibrate solves the camera system response from matched XP star spectra (SASpro stages 1-3, real Bayer throughput curve shapes from SASP_data.fits — identity curves are degenerate and desaturate to gray-world; SONY_COLOR_SENSOR UVIRCUT set for broadband, SONY_CMOS x L-eNhance set for LP) and applies the Stage-2 quadratic gains; SessionResponseCache seeds the next solve (verified: IC 1805 second run seeded from prior ctrl_points). Quality gate: applied-stage (Stage 2 sigma-clipped) RMS < 2.0, mirroring SASpro's own prior-trust threshold. (4) LP routing: color_calibration on LP data now tries SSSC FIRST (LP previously had no valid calibration — SPCC's broadband white reference is wrong for dual-narrowband); any SSSC failure falls through to the legacy PI SPCC/CC path unchanged. SSSC success writes .sssc_applied and counts as calibration success for the SCNR-skip and linked-stretch rules. SSSC results are exempt from the whole-frame SNR objective gate and get the lenient catastrophic-only stats-veto floor: the solved per-channel gains (k_R ~2.26 on LP) legitimately shift the SNR metric, which vetoed a correct calibration on the first live integration run (IC 1805, SNRx0.81 vs the 0.90 gate); the real quality check is the solver's applied-stage RMS < 2.0 gate (crop-exemption precedent: don't second-guess a deliberate transform with whole-frame stats). Broadband SSSC ships EXPERIMENT-ONLY this version (M 13 side-by-side showed a green core shift vs SPCC's neutral; default flip deferred to C3 validation = separate bump + canary re-baseline). Also fixes a latent gate bug: LP detection now happens ONCE on the source stack header — the crop step strips FILTER from run-dir intermediates, so the old mid-pipeline header sniffs would have silently no-opped on every real run. nb_palette black-sky fix (2026-06-12): per-channel background anchoring (sky->0 pre-stretch, re-anchored post) + signal-high-percentile midtone (not sky median), so composited palette sky is black instead of navy/teal; synthetic proof sky=[0,0,0]. Extreme-flux-ratio fallback NB_PALETTE_MAX_FLUX_RATIO=20: Ha/OIII ratio > 20 means OIII is a noise pedestal (IC 1805 ratio 157, OIII contrast 0.89 vs Ha 3.06) -> skip nb_palette, fall back to narrowband_norm; nb_palette is for genuine bicolor only.
versions.rationale: The SeeStar 'LP' filter is dual-narrowband (Ha 20nm + OIII 30nm), but the NBN branch only approximated channel separation (ha_dominance_ratio, Ha~R / OIII~B) and LP data got no real color calibration. SASpro 1.18.0 (promoted 2026-06-11, canary bit-identical) shipped NBExtract and SSSC; Henry's scope decisions: full narrowband workflow (extract H/O early in linear, synthesize S, composite SHO/HOO/Foraxx) and SSSC for both LP and broadband with broadband default flip gated on validation vs SPCC. Verified headless: xp_stars selftest (synthetic mixing-matrix recovery corr 1.0, NNLS reconstruction, synthetic R(lambda) solve rms 0.0015); IC 1805 LP end-to-end (280 XP stars, Stage 3, applied RMS 0.888, cache-seeded second run); M 13 broadband (84 stars, Stage 2, RMS 0.586). Old-drizzle stacks (1.19"/px WCS/row-order mismatch) no-op the XP machinery by design — the star-match gate fails closed.

changes.change: NEW shared Gaia-XP plumbing: detect_stars (SEP), match_xp (WCS px->sky -> find_nearest_batch, reproj dist^2<9 gate), measure_rgb (SASpro raw-aperture photometry), enrich_for_nbextract (line-window integrals + template class), enrich_for_sssc (S_star integrals over REAL Bayer throughput curves on sssc._WL_GRID; xp_flux Stage-3 compatible), load_throughput_curves (SASP_data.fits, nm->Angstrom), gather_calibration_stars, probe + --selftest CLI
NEW HOO/SHO/Foraxx compositor for extracted Ha/OIII: joint normalization, linked-by-luminance (or per_channel) statistical stretch, synthetic SII = s_mix*Ha (default 0.8), Foraxx dynamic G mix

NEW wrappers: xp_fit_matrix / xp_apply_matrix (two-phase NBExtract), nb_palette, sssc_calibrate (solve+apply, SessionResponseCache prior seeding + save, applied-stage RMS<2.0 gate, .sssc_applied sentinel, stage/RMS/bv_span/session diagnostics); spcc wrapper routes spcc_lp_filter=True -> SSSC first, legacy PI SPCC/CC fallback unchanged

versions.summary: background_neutralize blue-cast fix. (1) The completeness pass now measures the FOUR DARK CORNERS — the same region image_analyzer gates the step on — instead of the single auto-detected 50x50 patch. On frame-filling targets (IC 1805 — the Heart fills the centre) the auto-patch lands on an already-neutral spot while the dark corners carry the cast (IC 1805 corner sky B/R 1.25 survived the patch neutralize), so the step was a no-op and the blue cast reached the final. Corner-anchored per-channel offset now drives the corner sky to neutral grey (verified: IC 1805 corner B/R 1.25->1.00, G/R 0.95->1.00 in all three pivot modes). (2) _objective_check now gates background_neutralize on sky-cast improvement (cast_drop>0.02, SNR hold) instead of gradient drop. A colour step does not change the gradient, so the shared background_extraction gate (grad_drop>0) rejected EVERY neutralize when the gradient was already flat (IC 1805: 'gradient 1.000->1.000 0% drop' -> rejected) — the step could never apply. background_extraction keeps its gradient gate + the introduces-a-cast reject guard, now in its own branch.
versions.rationale: IC 1805 1.9.0 final carried a measured corner blue cast (B/R 1.26) that desaturated the Ha toward brownish-red; Henry flagged it. Root cause was two compounding bugs in the neutralize path: it sampled the wrong region (an auto-patch that read neutral) and its accept gate demanded a gradient drop a colour step can never deliver. M51/M13 corners are already neutral post-SPCC (no-op) but M42 has a mild residual corner cast that the working neutralize now corrects -> golden-baseline change on M42 -> MINOR + canary re-baseline with Henry's M42 before/after sign-off.

changes.change: background_neutralize completeness pass measures the four dark corners (m=max(h//20,w//20,50)) instead of the auto_rect_50x50 patch; subtracts per-channel offset to drive the darkest-corner channel reference (trigger _imbal>0.05). Neutralizes the cast region image_analyzer actually reads.

_objective_check: split background_neutralize into its own branch gated on sky-cast improvement (cast_drop>0.02 and SNR>0.85; metrics['sky_cast']); background_extraction keeps the gradient gate + sky-cast-WORSENED reject guard.

versions.summary: Register SSSC as an EXPERIMENT-ONLY color_calibration variant (cc_sssc) in processing_ontology.json. Broadband default stays SPCC; LP/dual-band default stays SSSC (1.9.0). Classified PATCH because no good-run output changes: this is an additive optional capability, not a default flip. A future broadband default flip to SSSC would be a separate MINOR + canary re-baseline.
versions.rationale: C3 broadband validation (2026-06-21) ran SSSC vs SPCC on five targets: M 13 (84 XP stars), NGC 188 (45), M 3 (31) all ran and tied SPCC's corner-sky neutrality within ~0.01-0.03; M 51 (15 stars) and M 42 (5) fell below the 20-star gate and fell back to SPCC. Conclusion: SSSC broadband only fires on star-rich fields and offers no improvement over SPCC where it runs, so it is not worth making the broadband default — but it is registered as an experiment variant so it can be A/B'd on star-rich targets. Henry chose 'experiment only' 2026-06-21.

PATCH: a small accuracy correction to one constant; affects BXT manual-PSF diameter by ~7%, no scoring-model or step change.

versions.summary: Nebula stretch-picker cost function: separate sky-placement from highlight-health so grain actually breaks ties. The nebula _neb_key previously lumped under+blown (highlight health) into the same 'placement' term as sky-band distance at 0.02 resolution; on faint LP nebulae the large/variable `under` term spread candidates across many buckets, so the grain tiebreaker never fired and the most aggressive/grainiest in-band stretch won (critique batch: stf/veralux beating cleaner stat/stat_bright at equal sky placement, e.g. IC 1805 veralux_strong grain 0.808 winning over stat 0.165). New key = (sky_bucket@0.02, health_bucket@0.05, grain, pref): sky placement primary (un-fixable downstream on Ha corners), highlight health a COARSE secondary, grain the real tiebreaker.
versions.rationale: Surfaced by the daily critique-pending pass (cross-batch signal across M 42 + IC 1805 LP-nebula runs). Validated with a read-only A/B harness (scripts/stretch_picker_ab.py) over 21 latest nebula runs: 9 change pick — 7 to a cleaner variant (NGC 6914 grain -0.301, NGC 2244 -0.261, IC 5146 -0.067, SH2-101 -0.060, SH 2-273 -0.026, IC 1396 -0.008, NGC 7000 -0.011), 2 to a better-EXPOSED but grainier variant (M 57 +0.085, NGC 6334 +0.102) where highlight health legitimately differs. MINOR: changes stretch selection output but not the scoring model or steps, so scores stay comparable. Galaxy/globular branches untouched. Golden M 42 pick is unchanged (still stf) per the harness.

changes.change: _physics_pick_stretch nebula branch _neb_key: was (round((bg_dist+under+blown+folio_dist)/0.02), grain, pref); now (round((bg_dist+folio_dist)/0.02), round((under+blown)/0.05), grain, pref).
New read-only A/B harness: recomputes current vs proposed nebula picker key over each target's latest nebula run and tables the pick deltas + grain change.

versions.summary: Preserve the celestial WCS through the color_calibration step. The PI color-cal path (run_postprocess) drops the astropy-readable WCS from its output; the preview renderer flips the image to north-up from the WCS (CDELT2 sign), so a WCS-less color_calibration output renders VERTICALLY FLIPPED vs the WCS-bearing upstream stages — the 'image orientation changes/looks wrong after color calibration' bug Henry caught on M 42. New _preserve_celestial_wcs(src,dst) re-injects the input WCS cards into the color-cal output when missing (no-op if a real WCS is present); called at all three spcc() success returns (sssc / spcc / pi_cc_fallback). M 42 hits this because it is drizzled (1.19"/px) → SSSC no-ops → PI SPCC/CC fallback, which is the WCS-dropping path. Empirically verified: WCS-injected color-cal preview matches the background_extraction preview as-is (corr 1.000) instead of flipud (1.000).
versions.rationale: Orientation/metadata bug fix. The final SCORED pixels are unchanged (WCS is header + preview rendering); the golden M 42 is drizzled so downstream xp/nb matching no-ops there regardless → golden output unaffected. PATCH. Note: on NATIVE nebulae this restores a usable WCS after color-cal, which may re-enable downstream WCS-dependent xp/nb behavior that was silently no-op'ing — a latent improvement, monitor on the next native-nebula runs. Takes effect on the next seestar.service restart (deferred — the M 42 canary + 9 stretch-picker requeues are mid-run on the old code).

changes.change: Added _preserve_celestial_wcs(src,dst); called before each successful return in spcc() (sssc, spcc, pi_cc_fallback). Copies CTYPE/CRVAL/CRPIX/CD/PC/CDELT/CROTA/CUNIT + WCSAXES/LONPOLE/LATPOLE/EQUINOX/RADESYS from input→output when the output lacks a WCS.

versions.summary: Bounded mid-run stretch vision tiebreak — DEFAULT OFF pilot (settings.stretch_vision_tiebreak, default false). When enabled, the nebula stretch picker, on a genuine close call (top two share the same sky AND exposure bucket, so grain alone separated them), makes ONE cheap Haiku vision compare of the two variant previews and lets it break the tie; any failure / physics-only keeps the physics pick. This targets exactly the aesthetic call physics is weakest at (the M 57 grain-vs-placement case from the faithful A/B) without re-scoring any step. Default behaviour is unchanged (flag off → zero API calls, identical picks). PATCH: opt-in capability, no default-run output change (cf. the experiment-variant additions 1.10.1/1.10.2).
versions.rationale: Henry approved a bounded mid-run feedback loop using a cheap vision API call (NOT the headless skill mechanism, which is reserved for the deferred weekly batch-eval — latency/quota). Shipped default-off as a pilot per the faithful-harness discipline: enable on a few targets, compare finals + verify picks before making it default. Pairs with the deferred loop (1.11.x critique-batch-eval) — the two halves of the critique feedback system.

_physics_pick_stretch gains vision_tiebreak param (default False) + close-call detection (same sky/health bucket on top two) → calls the vision tiebreak; added _stretch_preview_path helper. Caller reads settings.stretch_vision_tiebreak (default False).
Documented stretch_vision_tiebreak (default false).

versions.summary: Narrow colour-swap in the nebula stretch picker: Henry's taste = maximise colour SUBJECT TO clean. The picker already honoured 'clean' (lands on colourful-clean stat variants) but never reached for colour when freely available, so it could ship a desaturated stretch (M 42 stf) when a comparably-clean, more-colourful one (mas) existed. After the physics pick, SWAP only to a candidate that is comparably clean (bg_noise σ ≤ 1.2× the winner — GRAIN stays a hard constraint; Henry consistently rejected grainy veralux even when more colourful), well placed (under≤0.15, sky 0.02..wash), AND meaningfully more saturated (mean signal saturation ≥ winner + 0.05); take the most saturated qualifier. New _variant_saturation() helper; scored entries now carry the FITS path.
versions.rationale: Grounded in measurement + 7 blind labels (scripts/stretch_reframe_prototype.py, stretch_tiebreak_phase1.py journey): colour is largely IRRECOVERABLE downstream (M 42 color_boost closed <30% of the stf->mas sat gap), while grain is a hard reject for Henry (rejected veralux on IC 5146/NGC 7000/NGC 6914 despite more colour). The narrow rule reproduces 6/7 blind labels and changes ONLY M 42 (stf->mas), leaving the 5 correct picks untouched. Galaxy branch untouched (already mas-first via _GAL_PREF). MINOR: changes stretch selection, not the scoring model/steps.

versions.summary: Extend the WCS-preservation fix (1.11.1) to EVERY step, not just color_calibration. versions.summary: Sky-adaptive, signal-aware contrast recovery for nebulae (docs/spec_contrast_recovery.md). The 1.12.0 colour-first pick (mas) has a brighter sky that softens contrast; this downstream step (in the combine tail, where galaxies get sky_mute and nebulae were previously skipped) pulls the black point to darken the sky (M42 0.125->0.045) and steepens midtones with a SHADOW-PROTECTED S-curve — identity below the faint floor (sky+3sigma), steepen only above — so the faint Ha/OIII is NOT crushed (validated: 0.0% faint pixels crushed). Hue-preserving (channel scale by luminance ratio; M42 sat 0.406->0.509). Gated to bright-sky/soft picks (sky>=0.08; no-op on dark stf-type), strength depth-scaled (gentle on thin stacks).
versions.rationale: Completes the recoverability strategy: pick colour at the stretch (irrecoverable), recover contrast+sky downstream (recoverable). Henry: mas 'vibrancy better but contrast less... slight too much crushing' on the crude prototype -> shadow-protected version fixes the crush. MINOR: gated downstream behaviour change, scores comparable; nebula only (galaxy already sky_muted).

versions.summary: Frame-fill false-positive fix (M 1, grader 3.2). M 1 (6' Crab remnant in a dense Taurus star field) triggered frame_fill=True (coverage 0.93) — the smoothed 'coverage' was unresolved stars + noise, not emission. The dark-anchor over-brightening then amplified a residual gradient into a broad green band across the frame (grader: 'severe gradient contamination, broad horizontal green band'). The pixel tests CANNOT separate this case: M 1 and IC 1805 both measure corner_median/dark_floor = 1.04 pre-stretch. Fix: angular-size gate — a target < 30' cannot fill the 43'x77' S50 frame, so frame_fill is ineligible regardless of pixel coverage (folio angular_size_arcmin threaded from planner._folio_info). Validated: M 1 (7') ineligible, NGC 7000 (120')/IC 1805 (150') still fire. Unknown size falls through to pixels (no regression). NOTE: the horizontal BANDS Henry flagged in the on-device EAA live-stacks (Stacked_N files) do NOT reach the pipeline — Siril sigma-clip rejection over 3000+ subs removes the satellite trails at the pixel level (verified: pipeline raw stack trail check 3.1sigma, clean). The green band was created IN PROCESSING by the frame_fill mis-fire, not inherited from subs.

versions.summary: Grain-DQ scoped to GALAXIES only (SH 2-273 regression fix). The 1.21.0 absolute grain disqualifier (bg_noise > 0.10 drops a stretch candidate) was branch-neutral, but on faint nebulae the CORRECT brighter stretch is necessarily grainier — the DQ killed it and left a conservative dark pick, over-darkening the faint signal. Measured: SH 2-273 (Fox Fur/Cone) regressed 6.8 (v1.20.1, picked stat_bright) -> 4.5 (v1.22.1, DQ dropped stat_bright -> ghs_soft won -> 'faint nebulosity almost entirely absent'). The galaxy branch NEEDS the DQ (it ignores grain by design, 1.7.0 — that let veralux_strong win M 108 at 26x cleanest); the nebula branch already treats grain as a placement-equal tiebreaker, the right discipline for faint signal (feedback-faint-nebula-too-dark). Fix: apply the DQ only when is_galaxy. Validated on the saved candidates: SH 2-273 -> stat_bright (restores the 6.8 pick); M 108/NGC 4565 galaxies keep clean picks with veralux_strong still DQ'd. Found by the reprocess campaign (1 of ~20 wave-1 reprocesses regressed).

versions.summary: Small-target compositional recenter-crop (M 1 under-framed 2026-07-15). The coverage-driven crop step only trims blank/edge borders, so a target much smaller than the S50 frame ships as a speck in empty sky (M 1 6' filled ~10% of a 77'x43' field; grader: 'small relative to the field, low fill factor'; processing was otherwise good at 7.0). New _small_target_recenter_crop wraps the crop fn when the folio angular size < 11' (25% of the 43' short axis) AND there is no saved/reviewed crop (a user's manual framing stays authoritative — feedback-never-veto-crop). It locates the target as the brightest EXTENDED (non-star) blob via median+gaussian smoothing (robust — a fresh plate solve on the final gave inconsistent WCS), MEASURES the blob radius (95th-pct of half-peak pixels), and crops to 4.5x radius centered on it with a 240px native-res floor (no-overcrop rule). Sizing from the measured blob is scale-free — necessary because drizzled finals (~1.19"/px) are not reliably inferable from frame dimensions. Triggers: M 1 (7'), M 57 (2.5'), M 76, M 27 (8'), M 97 (3.4'), NGC 6826 (0.45'), M 105 (5.4'), small galaxies; skips M 51 (11.2'), M 31, M 42, IC 1805. Validated on M 1: Crab centered, cropped 2032x3712 -> 784px, full framing with margin.
